interface.title: CAVE FRF — CAVE Gain / Phase Analysis (Streamlit, v0.4)
interface.field: Biomechanics / vestibular and concussion rehabilitation research (postural control, visual-perturbation sway analysis)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis of collected force-plate and motion-capture trials: batch signal processing, group comparison, and export for statistics
interface.what_it_is_for: Point it at a folder of per-subject standing (COP) and walking (COM) trial files from the CAVE sum-of-sines visual-perturbation protocol, and it computes gain, phase and coherence at each stimulus frequency plus RMS, path-length and velocity sway metrics, then shows them as bar, recovery-trajectory, Nyquist and spectra plots and as CSVs to download.

data.note: I typed the server-side sample folder /work/app/sample_data/CAVE_Demo_Data (16 files: 6 COP standing, 10 COM walking, Control_001 Acute and SubAcute) and used the bundled trial-order file Updated-_CAVE_Adult_Stimulus_Factor_Trial.txt. I loaded configs/demo_quickstart.yaml first (one stimulus component at 0.5 Hz, 5 s trials). Both planted edge cases behaved as described. The spike in standing Acute_8 shows up clearly: gain 0.66 against about 0.03 elsewhere, coherence 0.29, and inflated AP RMS and path length. The NaN in walking SubAcute_3 still gave finite results (gain 0.048, coherence 0.98). As a deliberate wrong input, I also uploaded README_SYNTHETIC_DATA.txt in place of the trial-order file. Caution for statistics: summary_metrics.csv is meant to have one row per trial, but the replay's file had 28 rows for 16 trials, with the standing trials duplicated. The Summary row-count caption also varied across re-runs (32, 26 and 28 rows for 16 or 14 trials). De-duplicate on trial before analysis.

features.name: Data-folder discovery with an inventory breakdown
features.general: Type a path to a folder tree of recordings. The tool walks it, reports how many files of each kind it found, warns if the path is wrong, and shows a count table by condition, file type, group and timepoint so you can confirm nothing is missing before processing.
features.specific: Path to top-level CAVE Data folder → 'Found N data files (x COP / standing, y COM / walking)' or 'Folder does not exist' → expand 'Breakdown by condition / file type / group / timepoint'
steps: type the folder path and press Enter
read the found-files count (or the red missing-folder error)
expand the breakdown table to check counts per condition/group/timepoint
optionally point at a subfolder to analyse a subset
serves_tasks: Point the tool at the recordings and confirm every expected file was found
Re-run after the data set changes, reusing earlier results

features.name: Swappable protocol configuration file
features.general: Keep the stimulus parameters in a small config file and load a different one to fit another lab's protocol. The panel shows the formula and the name of the active config. The parameter list shown did not refresh after a load.
features.specific: Sidebar ⚙️ Stimulus configuration: D(t)=A·Σ wᵢ sin(2π fᵢ t+φᵢ), the parameter list, Path to YAML config, Load config, 'Loaded:' confirmation and 'Active config:' name
steps: expand ⚙️ Stimulus configuration
type the YAML path (e.g. configs/demo_quickstart.yaml or configs/example_other_lab.yaml)
press Load config
check 'Loaded:' and the Active config name
re-run the analysis so results use it
serves_tasks: Choose the protocol parameters that match the recordings

features.name: Trial-condition lookup: bundled default or upload
features.general: Give the table that maps each recording to its experimental level, either the built-in default or your own uploaded file. Trials missing from the table are left out of the run. An uploaded file is not checked when it is loaded, so a wrong file only shows up at run time.
features.specific: 1 — Trial-order file: 'Use bundled file' checkbox or Upload a TXT; the status line says 'Using bundled:' or 'Loaded:'
steps: leave 'Use bundled file' checked, or uncheck it
press Upload and choose a .txt trial-order file
check the status line
run; if nothing matches you get 'No trials matched the filter'
serves_tasks: Supply the table that maps each trial to its stimulus level

features.name: Filtered batch run
features.general: Choose which subset of trials to process (condition, whether to include no-stimulus baselines), run the batch, and get a count of trials and output rows.
features.specific: 3 — Analyze: Condition radio (standing/walking/both), 'Include amp=0 baseline trials', ▶ Run analysis → 'N trials from M subjects analyzed' and the 'FRF: … rows. Summary: … rows.' caption

toggle 'Include amp=0 baseline trials'
press ▶ Run analysis
read the trial and row counts (or the 'No trials matched the filter' warning)

features.name: Per-level gain and phase bars with axis switch
features.general: Bar charts of response gain and phase lag for each stimulus level at each stimulus frequency, with a switch for which measurement axis to analyse and a fullscreen view.
features.specific: Plot options: Analysis axis (stim_matched/AP/ML), Plot style 'Bar (per-trial)', 📊 Gain & Phase tab, chart Fullscreen button
steps: choose Analysis axis
choose Plot style 'Bar (per-trial)'
read gain and phase per amplitude in 📊 Gain & Phase
open the chart fullscreen to read it
serves_tasks: Inspect response gain and timing lag at each stimulus frequency, per stimulus level

features.name: Group × timepoint sway-metric comparison
features.general: Bar charts of sway amplitude, path length and speed for each axis, grouped by subject group and timepoint with standard-error bars, with a switch for which task condition to show.
features.specific: 📋 Summary metrics tab with 'Summary metrics — which condition?' (walking/standing): RMS, path length and mean velocity in AP and ML, Control vs Concussion, Acute vs SubAcute
steps: open 📋 Summary metrics
choose walking or standing
compare the bars and SEM across timepoints and groups for each metric and axis

features.name: Sortable, searchable group-means table
features.general: A table of averaged results per group, condition, timepoint, level, frequency and axis. Sort any column to bring extremes to the top and search to highlight matching cells.
features.specific: 📑 Group means table: columns group, condition, timepoint, amplitude_m, frequency_hz, axis, n_trials, gain, phase_deg, coherence; click a header to sort; toolbar Search, Show/hide columns, Download as CSV, Fullscreen
steps: open 📑 Group means table
click a column header (e.g. gain) to sort
press Search and type a term to highlight matches
optionally hide columns or download
serves_tasks: Read the group averages as numbers and find extreme values

features.name: Tidy CSV export of per-trial results
features.general: Two download buttons give long-format tables ready for statistics software: one row per trial × frequency × axis for the response measures, and one row per trial for the sway metrics. In this run the sway-metrics file contained duplicated trial rows, so check it before use.
features.specific: 📥 FRF results → frf_results.csv; 📥 Summary metrics → summary_metrics.csv; a caption shows the row counts
steps: run the analysis
press 📥 FRF results
press 📥 Summary metrics
check summary_metrics.csv for duplicate trial rows, then open the CSVs downstream
serves_tasks: Save the per-trial response measures and sway metrics as spreadsheets

features.name: Recovery-trajectory plot of the frequency response
features.general: Gain and phase plotted against recovery timepoint, one line per group × stimulus level, with standard-error bars. It can be shown alone or stacked under the per-level bars.
features.specific: Plot style 'Hwang-style (recovery)' or 'Both' → 'FRF recovery trajectory … error bars = SEM' (Acute → SubAcute → Chronic on x, Control/Concussion × amplitude lines)
steps: choose Plot style 'Hwang-style (recovery)' or 'Both'
choose Analysis axis
read gain and phase change across timepoints for each group and amplitude, with SEM
serves_tasks: Follow how the response changes across recovery stages

features.name: Frequency-response diagnostics: coherence, complex-plane and spectra views
features.general: Three checks on the quality of the response estimate: coherence bars (0–1) per stimulus level, a polar plot of each trial's response in the complex plane, and per-trial response spectra with the stimulus frequencies marked. Use them to spot outlier trials and artifacts.
features.specific: Tabs 📊 Coherence, 🎯 Nyquist ('FRF in complex plane'), 📈 Spectra (COP_AP spectra; the markers showed the default 0.16–0.49 Hz rather than the loaded config's 0.5 Hz)
steps: open 📊 Coherence and look for low-coherence levels
open 🎯 Nyquist and look for outlying points
open 📈 Spectra and look for off-stimulus peaks
reopen the tab after changing a plot option (it resets to Gain & Phase)
serves_tasks: Judge how reliably the response is driven by the stimulus
See gain and phase together as points in the complex plane
Check each trial's frequency content for artifacts

features.name: Incremental re-run cache
features.general: An option meant to reuse results already computed for unchanged recordings when re-running on a changed data set. In this run it merged cached trials from outside the current folder into the results and gave summary row counts larger than the trial count.
features.specific: 'Skip already-processed trials' checkbox (tooltip: 'Reuses results from the previous run for trials that haven't changed…') with ▶ Run analysis
steps: check 'Skip already-processed trials'
change the folder or add data
press ▶ Run analysis
compare the trial count and FRF/Summary row counts with the found-files count
serves_tasks: Re-run after the data set changes, reusing earlier results

screens_never_reached: The tool's main scientific use, comparing groups (Control vs Concussion) across all three timepoints (Acute, SubAcute, Chronic), was never shown. The legends list Concussion and the folder-layout hint shows Chronic/, but the sample data only has Control_001 at Acute and SubAcute, so no Concussion bars or Chronic points ever appeared.

Multi-frequency results (several stimulus components): the demo config has one 0.5 Hz component, and the 4-component CAVE default was not run because the 5 s sample files do not match its 120 s duration
The README's naming/layout warnings ('No CAVE data files found', type-vs-trial-number mismatch) and the Run button's disabled state before inputs are valid
not_done: I could not confirm that caching reprocesses only new trials. The UI never says how many trials were reused and how many were recomputed. With caching on, running on the Walking subfolder reported 14 trials (10 walking plus 4 cached standing trials from the previous run), which means cached results from outside the current folder get merged in. The Summary row-count caption also drifted (32, 26 and 28 rows for 16 or 14 trials). The replay found summary_metrics.csv at 28 rows for 16 trials, with duplicated standing trials. My earlier record of 16 rows is not supported.
Download as CSV from the Group means table toolbar did not produce a file I could read.

The sidebar parameter list (N components 4; 0.16/0.21/0.24/0.49 Hz; 120 s) never updated after loading a different config, even though the Active config name changed. The Spectra tab also marks the default 0.16–0.49 Hz frequencies instead of 0.5 Hz, so the displayed protocol parameters may not match the ones used to compute the results.

I did not test with a real, correctly formatted custom trial-order file. Only the bundled file and a wrong file (README) were tried; the wrong file was accepted without validation and only failed at run time with 'No trials matched the filter'.

Clicking the help icon next to 'Skip already-processed trials' also toggles the checkbox, so I turned caching off by accident and ran one uncached re-run because of it (caption: Summary 32 rows). That run is left out of the workflow.
After the config probe I re-loaded configs/demo_quickstart.yaml and re-ran (screens/059.webp) only to restore the earlier state; that step is left out of the workflow.
Changing a plot option resets the result tabs to Gain & Phase, so each view had to be reopened.
In the replay, the folder path field was redrawn mid-typing during a re-run, so one intended run used the previous path.
